text:
Priya Shah: quick flag — noticed our Dedicated reserved credits didn't reduce the ap-southeast-2 invoice for Feb. looks like the full amount hit cloud overage instead of the commit pool :confused:

Kai Chen: ugh. which invoice id? can you drop the invoice lines or a screenshot?

Priya Shah: invoice `INV-2026-02-DED-7890` — BillingBot summary below pasted from billing exports.

BillingBot: Invoice INV-2026-02-DED-7890 — total USD 62,314.00
  - Dedicated commit discount: $0.00 (expected -$4,800.00)
  - Promo/contract credits applied: $0.00 (expected -$2,500.00)
  - Cloud provider charges: $62,314.00
  - Ledger reference: ledger-2026-02-AU

Marta Lopez: did the commit pool recently change project mapping? last time this happened it was because the reserved capacity was attached to `redwood-ded-ap` while infra billing used `redwood-prod-ap` tag.

Zoe Bennett: I ran a quick check on the allocation job logs — looks like the credit-match worker errored on 2026-02-28 with a 400 from the billing API. snippet:
```
ERROR 2026-02-28T23:12:11Z credit-matcher service error: 400 Bad Request - account_id mismatch (expected: 0123-REDWOOD-AU, got: 0123-REDWOOD-AU-PROD)
queue: credit-matcher-alloc v2.4.1
```
Priya Shah: ok that explains it. the commit was created against the dedicated capacity pool `dedicated-ap-southeast-2-v2` and the cloud account on some projects has an extra suffix. seems like a tagging mismatch.

Kai Chen: can we apply a retroactive allocation? do cloud providers let us reapply promo/contract credits once the invoices are posted?

FinanceOps: Depends on provider. GCP usually allows an invoice adjustment if you file a support case with evidence that credits should have applied. AWS sometimes requires a billing dispute. We'll need the mapping, ledger IDs, and the reserved commitment contract id.

Marta Lopez: action items I suggest:
- Priya: open a provider billing case (GCP) referencing INV-2026-02-DED-7890 + ledger-2026-02-AU
- Kai: patch the credit-matcher to tolerate the extra suffix and re-run allocation for Feb
- Zoe: export the allocation-run logs + worker errors into the support bundle

Priya Shah: I'll open the GCP support case now. filing with the following details: commitment `COMMIT-AP-2026-042`, expected credit lines `-4800` (dedicated) and `-2500` (contract promo). attaching CSV of project -> account ids. :email:

Zoe Bennett: CSV preview I attached to the thread (sensitive data removed):
project_id,cloud_account_id,expected_credit_pool
redwood-prod-ap,0123-REDWOOD-AU-PROD,dedicated-ap-southeast-2-v2
redwood-data-ap,0123-REDWOOD-AU,commit-promo-ap

Kai Chen: small patch for matcher (will be in infra repo):
```
# tolerant matching: strip known suffixes from account id before compare
def normalize_account(a):
  return a.replace('-PROD','').replace('-STG','')
```
I'll run the reallocation job against Feb once PR merges. ETA ~3h. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

FinanceOps: once reallocation runs we'll need to produce a retro request to finance with the adjusted allocation CSV and the support case id. GCP will take ~3-5 business days to process adjustments if they accept the case.

Priya Shah: support case created: GCP-CASE-99234. included logs and allocation CSV. case owner assigned to GCP Billing team.

Marta Lopez: thanks. please add me to the case thread and drop any responses here. if GCP refuses, we'll prepare a manual invoice crediting plan (internal journal entries + customer ledger adjustments).

Zoe Bennett: reallocation job complete locally — it produced 1,412 matched lines, 27 unmatched (mostly new project suffixes). pushing patch now.

Kai Chen: patch merged, kicked reallocation job at 1975308659. will monitor.

BillingBot: reallocation run summary (1975308659): matched 1,412 lines, applied 0 retro adjustments (pending provider approval).

Priya Shah: noted. tagging: @Marta Lopez @Kai Chen @Zoe Bennett. I'll update when GCP replies. :eyes:

FinanceOps: flagged for month-end close — we'll add a hold on finalizing Feb ledger until GCP case resolves or internal journal is approved.

Priya Shah: closing loop for now — thanks team. follow-ups in #finance. :thumbsup:
